key_insight: HiFi-LLP predicts hardware latency with high accuracy and a confidence score, allowing HW-NAS to use cheap predictions when reliable and fall back to real measurements when needed.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the bottleneck of sequential hardware-in-the-loop evaluation, making edge-device neural architecture search faster while preserving deployment-quality decisions.
method: Graph attention network latency predictor trained on hardware/architecture graphs
Confidence metric to flag uncertain predictions
Hybrid NAS loop that sends low-confidence cases to hardware-in-the-loop evaluation
evidence_signal: Across six devices in LatBench, the predictor reaches up to 0.996 Spearman correlation and improves the 10% accuracy bound by up to 9 percentage points, with the hybrid NAS achieving up to 8.6× speedup.
watch_item: Performance depends on the target hardware and the quality of confidence calibration, so low-confidence routing may still require enough real measurements to avoid search bias.
paper_title: HiFi-LLP: High-Fidelity, Low-Cost Latency Predictors with Confidence for Robust HW-NAS
